body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm law}\), construct positive-multinomial null and alternative families on interior, source-boundary, box-boundary, and intersecting faces that preserve the two-sided exponent-\(a\) link and whose exact affinity matches every operator-fitting term generated by \(\mathsf H_{\rm prof}\). Which component of \(r_{\rm train}\) survives after the shared score of \(b\) and \(A\) is profiled out?
body.justification: This is the load-bearing converse that distinguishes the project from Gaussian analogy.
body.gap: No inspected inverse-testing or multinomial paper couples operator and regression perturbations while maintaining distance from a moving ellipsoid--box image.
body.consumer: A matched nuisance cost tells practitioners how much of the detection threshold is caused by learning the proxy operator.

obligation.what_is_open: A uniform lower-deviation and affinity calculation for the profiled moving image on every source, box, and intersecting face, with the joint training score for \(A\) and testing score for \(b\), is not closed.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen link condition controls singular magnitudes but permits arbitrary output rotations and supplies no tangent-cone stability bound. The legal dense family keeps the operator fixed, so it cannot certify which term of \(r_{\rm train}\) remains after joint profiling.
obligation.attempted: The proof decomposed the split distance against its oracle image, retained the exact Gram-metric perturbation, and examined a first-order source-face residual \(-\Delta A h_0\). These give a conservative upper cost but no matching positive joint-law mixture over all active faces.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved projection inequality gives the honest, unprofiled training contribution
\[
 R\sqrt{KS_\beta(K)/n_{\rm tr}}+
 \sqrt{K\log(2K)/n_{\rm tr}},
\]
while the fixed-support transverse path and the legal dense family above perturb only the regression component and therefore match neither summand.  At a fixed smooth source face, the first-order residual caused by an operator perturbation \(\Delta A\) is \(-\Delta A h_0\), so the bridge coefficient, not an inverse singular value, multiplies operator noise.  This is the strongest established reduction; uniform profiling over all source--box intersections and arbitrary output rotations remains unproved.
